conversation.content:
Hello! I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging that being a new mother can be a truly life-changing experience, and it's completely normal to have a wide range of emotions during this time. As part of our conversation today, I'll be administering the EPDS, which is a tool that helps us understand how you're feeling and if there are any concerns that we should address together.

The purpose of the EPDS is to screen for depressive and anxiety symptoms, as well as to check in with you about your overall well-being during the postpartum period. Please know that everything we discuss is completely confidential and is intended to create a safe and supportive space for you to express yourself honestly. I'm here to listen and support you, not to judge.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us get a better understanding of your emotional state over the past 7 days. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'll do my best to make this conversation feel as natural and comfortable as possible. Remember, this is a judgment-free zone, and your responses will help us tailor our support to your unique needs.

So, let's get started. The first question is: How have you been feeling about yourself and your life in general over the past week? Have you been able to enjoy the things that usually bring you happiness, or have you been feeling overwhelmed or down?

Honestly, it's been really tough. I feel like I'm just going through the motions most days. I'm exhausted all the time, and it's hard to find the energy to do anything, even things I used to love. Like, I used to enjoy reading and taking long baths, but now I just feel too tired to even think about those things. And when I do try to do something I used to enjoy, it just doesn't feel the same. It's like the happiness is just... muted, you know? 

I do get some pleasure from spending time with my baby, but even that can be overwhelming at times. I worry about everything - is she eating enough, is she safe, is she happy? It's like my mind is constantly racing with worst-case scenarios. And some days, it feels like the worries just consume me, and I feel really down and discouraged. I've even had some thoughts that feel really scary, like... like I'm not sure if I can do this, or if I'm cut out to be a mom. But those thoughts are really fleeting, and I try to push them away because they feel so overwhelming. 

I just feel really guilty a lot of the time, like I'm not doing enough or that I'm not good enough. And some days, it's hard to stop the tears. I cry when I'm stressed or feeling really overwhelmed, which is probably once or twice a week. But despite all of this, I'm trying to stay positive and focus on the good things, like my baby's smile or the way she cuddles with me. It's just... it's hard, you know?
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

I wish I could say that's been true for me, but to be honest, it's been a struggle to find the humor in things lately. I mean, I'll see something funny, like a meme or a video, and I'll think to myself, "Oh, that's funny," but it doesn't really make me laugh like it used to. It's like my sense of humor is just... dulled, I guess. And when I am around other people, like my family or friends, and they're laughing and joking, I feel like I'm just pretending to laugh along with them. It's hard to explain, but it feels like I'm just going through the motions, you know?

Sometimes, when I'm with my baby, I'll catch myself smiling or laughing at something she does, like when she makes a silly face or coos at me. But even those moments of joy feel... tainted, I guess, by all the worries and anxieties that are always lurking in the back of my mind. It's like I'm always waiting for the other shoe to drop, or for something to go wrong. And that makes it hard for me to really let go and just enjoy the moment, you know?

I do try to focus on the positive things, like when my baby sleeps through the night or when she learns something new. Those moments are really special to me, and they give me the strength to keep going, even on the tough days. But overall, it's just been really hard for me to find the funny side of things or to feel like myself lately.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

To be honest, I haven't really been looking forward to things like I used to. I mean, I'll think about upcoming events or activities, but instead of feeling excited or enthusiastic, I just feel... anxious, I guess. Like, I'll worry about how I'm going to manage with the baby, or whether I'll be able to get everything done that I need to do. It's hard to explain, but it feels like the joy has just been sucked out of things for me.

Even things that I used to love, like spending time with friends or trying new restaurants, just don't feel as appealing to me right now. I'll think about doing something fun, and then I'll just feel overwhelmed by all the logistics of making it happen with a new baby. Like, how will I get her to nap, or what if she gets fussy, or how will I even get out of the house on time? It's just too much, you know?

Sometimes, I'll have a moment where I'll think, "Oh, it would be nice to do this or that," but then the anxiety and worry just creep in, and it's hard for me to hold onto that feeling of excitement or anticipation. It's like, I'll think about taking a walk with my baby, and at first, I'll feel happy and looking forward to it, but then I'll start worrying about everything that could go wrong, and it just feels like too much effort.

I do try to make plans and look forward to things, though. Like, my husband and I will plan a date night, and I'll try to get excited about it, but even then, I'll just feel anxious about leaving the baby with a sitter, or worrying about whether I'll be able to relax and enjoy myself. It's just... everything feels so much harder and more complicated now, you know?
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes... I do that a lot, unfortunately. I feel like I'm always blaming myself for something, whether it's not being able to soothe the baby, or not being able to keep the house clean, or not being able to cook a decent meal. It's like, no matter what happens, I always manage to find a way to twist it around and make it my fault.

Like, the other day, my baby was crying and I couldn't figure out why, and I just felt like I was failing her. I thought to myself, "If I was a better mom, I would know what's wrong with her and I would be able to fix it." Or, if I'm having a tough day and I'm feeling overwhelmed, I'll think, "If I was more organized, or more patient, or more capable, I wouldn't be feeling this way."

It's hard for me to shake the feeling that I'm just not doing enough, or that I'm not doing things right. And even when my husband or family members try to reassure me and tell me that I'm doing a great job, I just can't seem to believe them. I feel like they're just being nice, or that they don't really understand what's going on.

Sometimes, I'll even catch myself thinking, "If I had just done this one thing differently, then maybe things would be better." Like, if I had just fed the baby more frequently, or if I had just put her down for a nap earlier, then maybe she wouldn't be fussing so much. It's like I'm always looking for ways to blame myself, and it's exhausting.

I know it's not rational, and I know that I'm being too hard on myself. But it's just really hard for me to break out of that pattern of thinking. It feels like it's just become a habit for me to assume that everything is my fault, and it's hard for me to remember that sometimes things just happen, and it's not always my fault.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes... that's me all the time, lately. I feel like I'm always on edge, waiting for something to go wrong. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just start worrying about something. Like, what if she chokes on something? What if she gets sick? What if I'm not doing enough to keep her safe?

It's like, my mind just starts racing with all these worst-case scenarios, and I can feel my heart racing and my palms getting sweaty. And the thing is, there's no reason for me to be worried. The baby is healthy, and she's thriving, and I'm doing everything I can to take care of her. But still, the worries just creep in.

Sometimes, I'll be lying in bed at night, and I'll just start thinking about all the things that could go wrong. Like, what if the house catches on fire? What if someone breaks in? What if I'm not able to protect the baby? It's like, my mind just starts spinning with all these terrible possibilities, and I feel like I'm paralyzed with fear.

And it's not just big things, either. I'll worry about little things, like, what if I forget to buy diapers? What if I run out of formula? What if the baby doesn't like the food I'm making for her? It's like, I'm just constantly on the lookout for potential disasters, and it's exhausting.

I try to calm myself down, I really do. I'll take deep breaths, and I'll try to focus on the present moment, and I'll remind myself that everything is okay. But it's hard to shake the feeling of anxiety, you know? It's like, it's just always there, lurking in the background, waiting to pounce.

Sometimes, I'll even find myself checking on the baby constantly, just to make sure she's okay. I'll get up in the middle of the night, and I'll go into her room, and I'll just stand there, watching her sleep, making sure she's breathing, making sure she's safe. And it's like, I know it's irrational, but I just can't help it. I feel like I have to be constantly vigilant, or something terrible will happen.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... I've been feeling that way a lot lately. It's like, I'll be going about my day, taking care of the baby, doing laundry, making dinner, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, my palms will get sweaty, and I'll feel like I'm going to hyperventilate. And it's not like anything specific is triggering it, it's just... out of nowhere.

Sometimes, it's when I'm alone with the baby, and I'll just start feeling overwhelmed by the responsibility of taking care of her. Like, what if something happens to me? What if I'm not able to protect her? What if I'm not doing enough for her? And then I'll start to feel this creeping sense of dread, like something terrible is going to happen.

Other times, it's when I'm in a crowded place, like the grocery store or the park, and I'll just feel like I'm going to lose control. Like, what if the baby gets sick? What if someone tries to take her from me? What if I get separated from her? And then I'll start to feel this intense anxiety, like I'm trapped and can't escape.

It's hard to explain, but it's like my body is just constantly on high alert, waiting for something to go wrong. And it's exhausting, because I'm always feeling like I'm walking on eggshells, just waiting for the other shoe to drop.

I've even had moments where I'll be holding the baby, and I'll just feel this sudden surge of fear, like I'm going to drop her or hurt her in some way. And it's not like I'm actually going to do anything to harm her, it's just... my mind is just playing these terrible scenarios over and over again, and it's hard to shake them off.

It's like, I know I'm a good mom, and I'm doing my best, but this fear and anxiety just keeps creeping in, and it's hard to know how to make it stop.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... that's exactly how I've been feeling. It's like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby, managing the household, trying to be a good partner and friend... it's all just feeling so overwhelming. I feel like I'm drowning in responsibilities, and I don't know how to stay afloat.

Some days, it feels like I'm just barely keeping my head above water. I'll get the baby to nap, and then I'll collapse on the couch, exhausted, and just feel like I'm waiting for the other shoe to drop. Like, what's going to happen next? What's going to go wrong? And then I'll start to worry about all the things I'm not doing, like laundry, or cleaning, or cooking... and it just feels like too much.

I've even started to feel like I'm losing myself in all of this. Like, I'm just a mom now, and that's it. I'm not a person, I'm not a wife, I'm not a friend... I'm just a mom. And it's a hard feeling to shake, because I know that being a mom is a big part of my identity now, but it's not the only part of me.

Sometimes, I'll look around the house, and I'll see all the mess, and all the things that need to be done, and I'll just feel like I'm going to cry. Like, how am I supposed to do all of this? How am I supposed to keep up? And then I'll start to feel guilty, because I know that I'm not doing enough, and that I'm not being the mom that I want to be.

It's like, I know I'm not alone in this feeling, but it's hard to remember that when I'm in the midst of it all. It feels like I'm the only one who's struggling, and that everyone else has it together. But deep down, I know that's not true. I know that everyone struggles, and that it's okay to not be okay. It's just hard to remember that when I'm feeling so overwhelmed.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... that's been me lately. I've been having a really hard time sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking me up at night. I mean, she does wake me up, but even when she's sleeping through the night, I'm still lying awake, feeling restless and anxious.

It's like, my mind just won't turn off. I'll be lying there, thinking about all the things I need to do, and all the things that could go wrong, and I just can't seem to calm down. I'll try to focus on my breathing, or try to relax my muscles, but it's hard to shake the feeling of unease that's been following me around.

And it's not just at night, either. I'll be awake during the day, feeling exhausted, but my mind will still be racing. I'll be thinking about all the things I need to do, and all the things I'm not doing, and it's just hard to feel like I'm doing anything right.

I've even started to feel like I'm walking around in a fog, like I'm just going through the motions of being a mom, but I'm not really present. And it's hard to connect with my baby, or my husband, or anyone else, when I'm feeling so disconnected from myself.

Sleep has always been a big deal for me, and I've always been someone who needs a lot of rest to feel good. But now, it's like I'm just surviving on fumes. I'll get a few hours of sleep here and there, but it's never enough. And it's not just the lack of sleep that's the problem, it's the feeling of being unhappy and unfulfilled that's keeping me awake.

I feel like I'm just trying to get through each day, without really living it. And that's a hard feeling to shake, because it feels like I'm just existing, rather than really being alive. But at the same time, I feel like I'm just trying to keep my head above water, and that's exhausting.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I feel like I'm just going through the motions of being a mom, but I'm not really feeling anything positive. I'm just feeling sad, and miserable, and overwhelmed all the time. It's like, I'll be sitting there, holding my baby, and I'll just start crying. And it's not just because I'm tired, or because I'm feeling overwhelmed, it's because I'm just feeling so sad.

I feel like I've lost myself in all of this. I'm not the same person I was before I had my baby. I'm not as confident, I'm not as carefree, I'm not as happy. And it's hard to remember what it was like to feel happy, to feel like myself.

I'll be doing things with my baby, like taking her for a walk, or playing with her, and I'll just feel this sense of sadness wash over me. It's like, I'm supposed to be enjoying this time with my baby, but I'm not. I'm just feeling sad, and anxious, and overwhelmed.

And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. Like, I'll be trying to get my baby to eat, and she'll just refuse, and I'll feel like I'm failing her. Or, I'll be trying to get her to sleep, and she'll just cry and cry, and I'll feel like I'm not doing anything right.

I feel like I'm just constantly questioning myself, and my abilities as a mom. And it's hard to shake the feeling that I'm not good enough, that I'm not doing enough. It's like, I'm just waiting for someone to tell me that I'm doing a good job, that I'm a good mom. But until then, I'm just stuck in this cycle of sadness, and self-doubt.

Sometimes, I'll have moments where I'll feel okay, where I'll feel like I'm getting the hang of this mom thing. But then something will happen, and I'll just feel like I'm back at square one. And it's hard to keep going, when I feel like I'm not making any progress, when I feel like I'm just stuck in this rut of sadness, and anxiety.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, I'll just be going about my day, and then suddenly I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of sadness and I'll start crying. It doesn't even have to be anything big that sets me off, just little things like the baby crying or my husband not understanding what I'm going through.

I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, or changing her diaper, and I'll just start crying. And it's not just a few tears, it's like, full-on sobbing. I'll be trying to calm myself down, but I just can't seem to stop crying. It's like, my body is just releasing all this pent-up emotion and I'm powerless to stop it.

Sometimes, I'll be crying and my husband will try to comfort me, but I just push him away. I don't want to be comforted, I just want to be left alone to cry. It's like, I need to just feel this sadness and let it wash over me.

I've even started to feel like I'm crying all the time. Like, I'll be crying in the shower, or while I'm driving, or even while I'm playing with the baby. It's like, I'm just constantly on the verge of tears and I don't know how to stop it.

It's hard to explain, but it's like, I'm just feeling so much emotion all the time and I don't know how to process it all. I'll be feeling happy one minute, and then sad the next, and it's just exhausting. I feel like I'm just constantly on an emotional rollercoaster and I don't know how to get off.

I've even started to feel like I'm a burden to my family and friends. Like, they're all trying to be supportive, but I just feel like I'm weighing them down with my constant crying and sadness. It's like, I want to be strong for them, but I just can't seem to be right now.

I just wish I could go back to being the happy, carefree person I used to be. But right now, I just feel like I'm stuck in this rut of sadness and I don't know how to get out of it.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

I... I don't know how to talk about this. It's just so hard to admit. But... yes, the thought of harming myself has occurred to me. It's not something I'm proud of, and it's not something I want to think about, but it's just been there, lurking in the back of my mind.

It's like, when I'm feeling really overwhelmed and sad, and I don't know how to make it stop, my mind just starts to wander to these dark places. And I'll think, "What if I just didn't exist anymore? Would anyone even notice?" Or, "What if I just ended it all, would it make everything better?"

It's not that I really want to hurt myself, it's just that the pain and the sadness feel so overwhelming, and I don't know how to make it stop. And in those moments, it feels like the only way to escape the pain is to just... disappear.

But at the same time, I know that's not true. I know that I have a baby who needs me, and a husband who loves me, and friends and family who care about me. And I know that I'm not alone, that there are people who can help me through this.

It's just... it's hard to shake the feeling that I'm a burden to everyone, and that it would be better if I just wasn't here. But deep down, I know that's not true. I know that I'm loved, and that I'm needed, and that I have so much to live for.

I just wish... I wish I could get out of this darkness, you know? I wish I could find a way to make the pain stop, and to feel happy again. I wish I could be the mom and the wife and the person I want to be, without all this weight holding me back.

I'm so sorry, I'm just... I'm really struggling right now. I feel like I'm barely holding on, and I don't know how much longer I can keep going like this.
